MerchantBrandOut.description:
One brand of the wholesale catalog, with its products.

``name`` is the catalog's default locale, like the product's; a brand
whose products all price out is absent entirely rather than empty.

category_name.description: That section's name, in the catalog's default locale.
category_name.title: Category Name

category_slug.description: Which storefront section this brand sits in — the same split a person sees on yupay.uz. `null` if it has none; the brand is still listed, because the price list's job is prices.
category_slug.title: Category Slug

hero_image_url.description: Wider brand artwork, an absolute URL, or `null`.
hero_image_url.title: Hero Image Url

logo_url.description: Brand artwork, an absolute URL — the same file the storefront renders. `null` where none is uploaded, so you can draw a placeholder instead of a broken image.
logo_url.title: Logo Url

name.description: The brand name, in the catalog's default locale.
name.title: Name

products.description: Products with at least one purchasable SKU. Never an empty shell.
products.title: Products

MerchantBrandOut.title: MerchantBrandOut

MerchantCatalogOut.description:
Body of ``GET /merchant/v1/catalog``: the whole B2B price list.

An object rather than a bare array so v1 clients keep parsing when a
future field (a cursor, a generated-at stamp) is added beside ``brands``.

brands.description: Every brand you can buy from, priced for your account.
brands.title: Brands

MerchantCatalogOut.title: MerchantCatalogOut

MerchantDeliveryOut.description:
The artifact a delivered order handed over — the voucher code lives here.

Present as soon as a ``deliveries`` row exists for the order — it is the
delivery record that decides, not the order's status, which is what
``order_status._delivery`` reads. The two normally move together.
``artifact``'s shape depends on ``artifact_kind`` (``voucher_code`` or
``topup_receipt`` today); for ``voucher_code`` it carries ``code`` (or
``codes``). Internal fields recorded alongside it — our supplier's name,
their order id, our warehouse row — are filtered out by
``fulfillment.buyer_safe_artifact``, the same allow-list the storefront
uses.

artifact.description: The delivered thing. For `voucher_code` it carries `code` (or `codes`). Internal fields — our supplier, their order id, our warehouse row — are never in here.
artifact.title: Artifact

artifact_kind.description: What was delivered: `voucher_code` or `topup_receipt`. It decides the shape of `artifact`.
artifact_kind.title: Artifact Kind

delivered_at.description: When it was handed over, ISO 8601 UTC.
delivered_at.title: Delivered At

MerchantDeliveryOut.title: MerchantDeliveryOut

MerchantFieldOut.description:
One input a product's ``fulfillment_data`` expects.

The machine API has always told an integrator that ``fulfillment_data`` is
required and never *what it takes* — that lived in prose, which means every
new product is a documentation round trip before a reseller can sell it.
This is the same schema the storefront renders its checkout form from,
trimmed to what a caller needs: the key to send, whether it is optional,
and the pattern we will validate against before anything is charged.

``label`` and ``placeholder`` are locale maps because the cabinet renders
them to a person; a machine caller can ignore both and read ``key``.

label.description: Locale → label, for your own UI. A machine caller can ignore it.
label.title: Label

pattern.description: The regex we validate against before anything is charged. Check it in your own form and save the round trip.
pattern.title: Pattern

placeholder.description: Locale → placeholder text, for your own UI.
placeholder.title: Placeholder

required.description: Whether the order is refused without it.
required.title: Required

type.description: What kind of value it is ("text", "number").
type.title: Type

MerchantFieldOut.title: MerchantFieldOut

MerchantOrderCreateIn.description:
Body of ``POST /merchant/v1/orders`` (spec §9.1).

One SKU per order, deliberately: a reseller's own basket does not have to
be ours, and a single line keeps "the order failed" from meaning "part of
the order failed". An ``items`` array can still be *added* later without a
``/merchant/v2`` — a new optional request field is additive; removing one
is not, which is the escape hatch ``quantity`` below was added through.

``extra="forbid"`` on purpose. On a response, ignoring an unknown field is
right; on a *request* it is how a typo'd ``fulfilment_data`` silently
becomes an order with no player id, delivered to nobody.

amount_usd.description: How many dollars of face value, on a `kind=amount` SKU. Required there and refused elsewhere, on the same no-silent-default rule as `quantity`. This is the **face value you are loading**, not what you pay: $100 of Steam wallet costs $104 at a 4% markup. Bounded by that SKU's `min_amount_usd` and `max_amount_usd`.
amount_usd.title: Amount Usd

expected_price.description:
The **order total** you last computed from `/catalog` — a fixed SKU's `price_usd`, or `ceil_to_cent(unit_price_usd × quantity_or_amount_usd)`.

A tolerance, **not a bid**: within ±2% of ours the order proceeds and is charged at *our* current price; outside it you get `422 price_changed` carrying that price, and you decide whether to re-send.
expected_price.title: Expected Price

fulfillment_data.description: Whatever the SKU's product requires — a player id, a login. The keys and their patterns are published on each product as `required_fields`. An undeclared key is **rejected**, not dropped, so a SKU that requires nothing accepts only `{}`.
fulfillment_data.title: Fulfillment Data

merchant_order_id.description: **Your** id for this order, and the idempotency key — send the same one again and you get the same order back, never a second charge. Printable ASCII with no spaces, so it survives being a path segment in `GET /merchant/v1/orders/{merchant_order_id}` and the signing string.
merchant_order_id.title: Merchant Order Id

quantity.description: How many units, on a `kind=unit` SKU. **Required** there and **refused** on the other shapes, both as a 422 — neither direction has a silent default, because a missing quantity would sell one Star and an ignored one would charge for a denomination you thought was ten. Bounded by that SKU's `min_qty` and `max_qty`.
quantity.title: Quantity

sku_id.description: From `GET /merchant/v1/catalog`. A UUID; any spelling of it is accepted.
sku_id.title: Sku Id

MerchantOrderCreateIn.title: MerchantOrderCreateIn

MerchantOrderEventOut.description:
One entry of an order's timeline.

``event`` only — no payload. An ``order_events`` payload carries internal
values (``order.paid``'s is a fingerprint of the reseller's own request;
``order.failed``'s is an operator's free-text note when support closed the
order by hand, and an internal label when the automatic refund closed it —
M3c Task 6), and none of them is worth a field on a third-party contract.

event.description: One of the published `order.*` kinds. Internal audit entries are omitted entirely, and a new kind stays omitted until it is documented.
event.title: Event

MerchantOrderEventOut.title: MerchantOrderEventOut

MerchantOrderOut.description:
Body of ``POST /merchant/v1/orders``.

``status`` is the order's live status, not a fixed ``"paid"``: a merchant
order is born paid and fulfilment starts in the same transaction, so what
comes back is where that left it. Poll
``GET /merchant/v1/orders/{merchant_order_id}`` for the rest.

created_at.description: When the order was placed, ISO 8601 UTC.
created_at.title: Created At

merchant_order_id.description: The id you sent. Key your records on it.
merchant_order_id.title: Merchant Order Id

order_id.description: Our id for the order. Quote it to support; key nothing on it.
order_id.title: Order Id

price_usd.description: What this order charged — **our** price at the moment you ordered, within ±2% of the `expected_price` you sent or it would have been refused. Fixed from here on: whatever fulfilment ends up costing us is our problem.
price_usd.title: Price Usd

status.description: Where the order is right now. See the order read.
status.title: Status

MerchantOrderOut.title: MerchantOrderOut

MerchantOrderStatusOut.description:
Body of ``GET /merchant/v1/orders/{merchant_order_id}``.

The reseller's whole view of one order: where it is, what it cost, what it
delivered, and whether anything came back. **This is the only place the
delivered voucher code is handed over** — the ``order.status_changed``
webhook (M3a, ADR-0070) does not carry it, because a webhook body lands in
the merchant's logs and in ours, and a voucher code is a bearer instrument.

created_at.description: When you placed it, ISO 8601 UTC.
created_at.title: Created At

delivered_at.description: When it was delivered, or `null` if it has not been.
delivered_at.title: Delivered At

delivery.description: What was delivered, once anything was. **The only place a code is given.**

failure_reason.description:
A closed vocabulary, additive only — never a supplier's or an operator's own words, because you cannot switch on prose.

- `null` — nothing has gone wrong.
- `fulfillment_delayed` — **not terminal.** Delivery has stopped; the order has not. Keep polling, do not re-order, do not refund your customer.
- `fulfillment_failed_refunded` — delivery failed and **all** of what you paid is back.
- `fulfillment_failed` — delivery failed; any refund is partial or pending.
- `order_failed` — support closed the order.

A loop that stops on `failure_reason != null` will stop polling an order we are about to deliver. Stop on the terminal values, not on the field.
failure_reason.title: Failure Reason

merchant_order_id.description: The id you placed the order with.
merchant_order_id.title: Merchant Order Id

order_id.description: Our id for the order. Quote it to support.
order_id.title: Order Id

paid_at.description: When the deposit was charged. A merchant order is born paid.
paid_at.title: Paid At

refunded_usd.description: How much of `price_usd` is back on your deposit. `"0.00"` until something comes back. Read from the ledger, so both an automatic refund and a settlement booked by hand land here. Never more than `price_usd`.
refunded_usd.title: Refunded Usd

sku_id.description: The SKU this order was placed against.
sku_id.title: Sku Id

status.description:
`paid` → `fulfilling` → `delivered`, or `failed`.

`failed` arrives two ways: support closing an undeliverable order, and a delivery failure whose **whole** charge is already back on your deposit. Read `failure_reason` to tell them apart. New values may be added — treat one you do not know as still in flight.
status.title: Status

timeline.description: What happened and when, oldest first.
timeline.title: Timeline

MerchantOrderStatusOut.title: MerchantOrderStatusOut

MerchantPlayerCheckIn.description:
Body of ``POST /merchant/v1/validate/player`` (spec §9.1).

``extra="forbid"``, for the same reason ``MerchantOrderCreateIn`` sets it:
on a request, silently ignoring an unknown key is how a typo'd
``player_id`` becomes a check of nothing that answers ``unsupported`` and
gets read as "this brand needs no verification".

brand.description: The brand you are about to order from, by its slug as listed in `GET /merchant/v1/catalog`. A brand and not a SKU, because a brand is one game (ADR-0079): the id you check here is the id every SKU of the brand credits.
brand.title: Brand

player_id.description: Your **end customer's** identifier — the game's player id, or the Steam login. We hold it for the length of the request and never write it to a log or a URL, which is why this endpoint is a POST.
player_id.title: Player Id

server_id.description: The game server or zone, for the games that ask for one. Send what the SKU's product declares and omit it otherwise — an empty string is refused rather than taken as a third spelling of "no server".
server_id.title: Server Id

MerchantPlayerCheckIn.title: MerchantPlayerCheckIn

MerchantPlayerCheckOut.description:
Body of ``POST /merchant/v1/validate/player`` — an **advisory** verdict.

Four outcomes, and the difference between them is the whole point of the
endpoint. Switch on ``status``; never treat "not ``invalid``" as approval.

* ``valid`` — the provider resolved the id. ``name`` carries the account
  nickname where the provider returns one (G2B does; Steam has no display
  name to give, so it stays ``null`` — an absence, not a placeholder).
* ``invalid`` — the provider answered and the id does not exist. This is
  the one answer that says your customer mistyped something.
* ``error`` — **we could not check.** An upstream fault, a timeout, a
  rejected credential of ours, or a circuit we opened after a run of
  failures. It says nothing at all about the id, so it must not be read as
  either approval or refusal; retry, or order without a check.
* ``unsupported`` — this SKU's product has no player check configured, and
  will not grow one on its own. Distinct from ``error`` because that one is
  worth retrying and this one never is.

Nothing here reports how the answer was reached, deliberately: a verdict
served from the 300 s cache is still our best answer, and a "this was
cached" caveat would only invite integrators to distrust a good one.

name.description: The account nickname, where the provider returns one. `null` is an absence, not a placeholder — some providers have no display name to give.
name.title: Name

status.description:
Switch on this. Never read “not `invalid`” as approval.

- `valid` — the provider resolved the id.
- `invalid` — the provider answered and the id does not exist. The one answer that means your customer mistyped something.
- `error` — **we could not check.** Says nothing about the id. Retry, or order without a check.
- `unsupported` — this product has no player check and will not grow one. Never worth retrying.
status.title: Status

MerchantPlayerCheckOut.title: MerchantPlayerCheckOut

MerchantProductOut.description:
One product of a brand, with its purchasable SKUs.

Only products with at least one purchasable SKU appear — there are no
empty shells to iterate past. ``name`` is the catalog's default locale
(``catalog.service.DEFAULT_LOCALE``, ``ru``); ``slug`` is the stable
machine-readable half and never changes with a translation edit.

name.description: The product name, in the catalog's default locale.
name.title: Name

required_fields.description: What every SKU under this product needs in `fulfillment_data`.
required_fields.title: Required Fields

slug.description: The stable machine-readable name. Never changes with a translation edit.
slug.title: Slug

MerchantProductOut.title: MerchantProductOut

MerchantProfileOut.description:
Body of ``GET /merchant/v1/me`` — who is calling, and what they can spend.

``balance_usd`` is the deposit ledger's signed posting sum
(``service.deposit_balance``), read live on every call — there is no
balance column to drift from it.

balance_usd.description: What you can spend right now, in USD. Summed from the deposit ledger on every call — there is no stored balance that could drift from it.
balance_usd.title: Balance Usd

merchant_id.description: Your account id. Quote it to support.
merchant_id.title: Merchant Id

status.description: `active`, or `frozen` while the account is suspended. A frozen account can still read, and every write answers `403 merchant_frozen`.
status.title: Status

title.description: Your company name, as it appears on your invoices.
title.title: Title

MerchantProfileOut.title: MerchantProfileOut

MerchantSkuOut.description:
One purchasable line of the wholesale price list.

``sku_id`` is what ``POST /merchant/v1/orders`` takes. Every price here is
THIS merchant's, not the retail one. ``updated_at`` is the SKU row's own
stamp, so a merchant polling the price list can tell what moved (spec §8.4
— there are no price webhooks).

**Two shapes, and ``kind`` says which.** A fixed SKU is a denomination:
one ``price_usd``, order one of it. A unit SKU is a currency sold by the
unit: a six-decimal ``unit_price_usd`` and a ``quantity`` on the order.
Exactly one of the two price fields is ever populated, because a machine
contract cannot hand a client two shapes for one quantity — and "price" on
a unit SKU is not one quantity but two, the per-unit rate and the total.

kind.description:
Which shape this line is, and therefore what to send beside `sku_id`:

- `fixed` — a denomination you buy one of. Nothing extra.
- `unit` — a currency counted in units (Telegram Stars). Send `quantity`.
- `amount` — a balance loaded in dollars (a Steam wallet). Send `amount_usd`.
kind.title: Kind

max_amount_usd.description: `kind=amount` only: the largest `amount_usd` we accept, inclusive.
max_amount_usd.title: Max Amount Usd

max_qty.description: `kind=unit` only: the largest `quantity` we accept, inclusive.
max_qty.title: Max Qty

min_amount_usd.description: `kind=amount` only: the smallest `amount_usd` we accept, inclusive, in dollars of face value. `unit_price_usd` is then the price of **one dollar** of that balance.
min_amount_usd.title: Min Amount Usd

min_qty.description: `kind=unit` only: the smallest `quantity` we accept, inclusive.
min_qty.title: Min Qty

name.description: The denomination, as a person would read it ("60 UC"). Falls back to `sku_code` for lines that carry none. The same string in every locale — denominations are not translated.
name.title: Name

price_usd.description: `kind=fixed` only: the order total, and what to send as `expected_price`. `null` on the other two shapes, which have no price until a quantity is chosen.
price_usd.title: Price Usd

retail_price_usd.description: What the same thing costs on yupay.uz — the reference your wholesale price is a discount against, so you do not have to match SKUs by hand. `null` on a `kind=amount` line, where retail is charged as a live FX rate times a margin and there is no single figure to quote.
retail_price_usd.title: Retail Price Usd

sku_code.description: Our internal code for the line. Useful in a support conversation.
sku_code.title: Sku Code

unit.description: `kind=unit` only: what one unit is, for your UI ("stars").
unit.title: Unit

unit_price_usd.description: `kind=unit` and `kind=amount`: the price of **one** unit at six decimals — one Star, or one dollar of wallet balance. Your total is `ceil_to_cent(unit_price_usd × quantity_or_amount)`, computed from this exact value, so you can reproduce your charge before you send it. `null` on a fixed line.
unit_price_usd.title: Unit Price Usd

updated_at.description: When this line last changed. Poll the catalog and compare it to tell what moved — there are no price webhooks.
updated_at.title: Updated At

MerchantSkuOut.title: MerchantSkuOut

MerchantTransactionOut.description:
One movement of the merchant's deposit.

``amount_usd`` is **signed**: positive credited the deposit, negative spent
it. The column adds up to the balance ``GET /merchant/v1/me`` reports.

amount_usd.description: **Signed**: positive credited the deposit, negative spent it. The column adds up to the balance `GET /merchant/v1/me` reports.
amount_usd.title: Amount Usd

created_at.description: When it was posted, ISO 8601 UTC.
created_at.title: Created At

kind.description:
- `merchant_deposit_credit` — we credited your deposit.
- `merchant_order_charge` — an order spent it.
- `merchant_order_refund` — we returned a failed order's charge.

More may be added. Treat an unknown kind as "some movement" and trust `amount_usd`.
kind.title: Kind

merchant_order_id.description: The same order's id in **your** system, so a statement line reconciles against your books without a second lookup.
merchant_order_id.title: Merchant Order Id

order_id.description: The order this movement belongs to, if any. Present on credits too — a settlement booked against a failed order is a credit that names it. `null` means an ordinary prepayment.
order_id.title: Order Id

transaction_id.description: Our id for this ledger entry.
transaction_id.title: Transaction Id

MerchantTransactionOut.title: MerchantTransactionOut

MerchantTransactionsOut.description: Body of ``GET /merchant/v1/transactions`` — one page, newest first.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `?cursor=` for the next, older page. `null` means this page is the last one — never call again on a null.
next_cursor.title: Next Cursor

MerchantTransactionsOut.title: MerchantTransactionsOut

MerchantKey.description: Your key id, `ypm_…`. Public; it identifies the key, not you.
MerchantKey.name: X-Merchant-Key

MerchantSignature.description: Lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical string, keyed by your secret. Send `X-Merchant-Timestamp` beside it.
MerchantSignature.name: X-Merchant-Signature

info.description:
Wholesale ordering for resellers.

**Every request is signed.** Send `X-Merchant-Key`, `X-Merchant-Timestamp` and `X-Merchant-Signature`, where the signature is HMAC-SHA256 over

```
{timestamp}\n{METHOD}\n{raw_path}\n{raw_query}\n{sha256_hex(body)}
```

keyed by your secret. The timestamp must be within ±300 s of ours. A signature is deliberately **not** single-use, so an at-least-once retry of the same request is safe.

**Money is a decimal string**, never a float — `"16.54"`. Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC. Fields are only ever *added* to a response, so parse leniently; a breaking change would be a `/merchant/v2`.

**Stuck?** Write to [@jama_omonov](https://t.me/jama_omonov) in Telegram.

**"Try it out" will not work here, and cannot.** Every call is signed with your merchant secret, and that secret belongs on your server — pasting it into a box on a web page would undo the one rule this whole auth design rests on. Ready-made cURL, Python and Node.js samples with the signature already computed are at [reseller.yupay.uz/docs](https://reseller.yupay.uz/docs); copy one into your own terminal, where your secret already lives.
info.title: YuPay Merchant API

get.description:
Return every B2B-visible, priced SKU with this merchant's price.

Visibility, pricing and the query shape are all
``price_list.build``'s — see that module. Every ``price_usd`` here is the
price this merchant would be charged; SKUs without a cost are absent
rather than free, and there are no price webhooks, so poll this and watch
each SKU's ``updated_at`` (spec §8.4).

401.description: Not authenticated. `code` is `missing_credentials` (a header is absent), `stale_timestamp` (not digits, or more than ±300 s from ours) or `invalid_credentials` (unknown key, revoked key, or a signature that does not match). The three are deliberately indistinguishable from outside beyond the code.

403.description: Authenticated and refused. `merchant_frozen` — the account is suspended; `ip_not_allowed` — this address is not on the key's allowlist.

schema.description:
The ``422`` a request the schema itself refused answers with.

Not raised anywhere — it exists so the OpenAPI document tells the truth for
this prefix. Every other surface answers a validation failure with
FastAPI's ``HTTPValidationError`` (``{"detail": [ … ]}``); ``/merchant/v1``
answers RFC 7807, because its error table is published to third parties
who cannot redeploy on our schedule. The renderer is
``core.errors.problem_json_validation_handler``, which is scoped to this
prefix for that reason and delegates everywhere else.

``detail`` is a **string** here, as RFC 7807 requires and as every other
error on this API already is; the per-field list FastAPI would have put
there rides in ``errors`` instead.

code.description: Always `invalid_request` here. Switch on this rather than on the status: every error on this API carries one, so no case is special.

post.description:
Buy one SKU against the prepaid deposit.

The whole flow — pricing, the ±2% drift rule, the margin floor, the
deposit debit, ``paid`` and the start of fulfilment — is
``merchants.orders.place``'s; this parses and dispatches. Idempotent on
``merchant_order_id``: the same id with the same body returns the order
already placed, a different body is a ``409``.

get.description:
Return one order's status, timeline, delivered artifact and refund mark.

Scoped to the authenticated merchant and to their own id — see
``merchants.order_status``, which also explains why an order belonging to
another merchant answers with the same 404 as one that never existed.

The path segment arrives percent-decoded, so an id containing ``/``
(legal, and in the README's worked example) is matched against the stored
value rather than split into route segments.

schema.description:
The ``422`` a request the schema itself refused answers with.

Not raised anywhere — it exists so the OpenAPI document tells the truth for
this prefix. Every other surface answers a validation failure with
FastAPI's ``HTTPValidationError`` (``{"detail": [ … ]}``); ``/merchant/v1``
answers RFC 7807, because its error table is published to third parties
who cannot redeploy on our schedule. The renderer is
``core.errors.problem_json_validation_handler``, which is scoped to this
prefix for that reason and delegates everywhere else.

``detail`` is a **string** here, as RFC 7807 requires and as every other
error on this API already is; the per-field list FastAPI would have put
there rides in ``errors`` instead.

get.description:
Return one page of the calling merchant's deposit movements.

Paging, the shared grouped query and why it is keyset rather than OFFSET
are all ``merchants.transactions``'. The merchant comes from the signature;
no parameter here names one.

Note that ``limit`` and ``cursor`` are part of the signed canonical string
(Task 2's fourth field, the raw query), so a signature does not carry
across a change of page.

post.description:
Verify a player id (or Steam login) for the brand you intend to buy
from — a brand is one game (ADR-0079), so the id you check is the id
every SKU of it credits.

Advisory, and never a fake approver (spec §9.1): ``valid`` and ``invalid``
are the provider's own verdict, ``error`` means we could not check and says
nothing about the id, and ``unsupported`` means this brand has no checker at
all. The rules, and why ``error`` may never render as ``valid``, are
``merchants.validate``'s; this parses and dispatches.

A ``POST`` although it writes nothing — the identifier must not travel in a
URL (spec §9.2) — so it takes no ``Idempotency-Key``; see the module
docstring.

**Two counters, both this endpoint's own**, charged after authentication
because the prefix-wide IP counter in ``merchant_auth`` has already turned
away anyone unauthenticated: one per source address, and one per
*merchant*. The second is not redundant — the quota being rationed is a
supplier's, which a reseller spends per account rather than per egress
node, so an address counter alone hands a multi-node NAT pool one budget
each. ``merchants.validate.charge_merchant_quota`` carries the argument.

``merchant`` is used for that counter and for nothing else: what a merchant
may *check* is a property of the catalog row (``brand.visible_b2b AND
sku.visible_b2b``), not of the caller.
